name: Youth Board Meeting - Jun 03, 2026
agenda_text:
City of Burbank
  Youth Board
  Agenda

  Wednesday, June 3, 2026
  6:00pm

  Community Services Building
  Community Room #104
  150 North Third Street
  Burbank, CA 91502

This agenda contains a summary of each item of business which the Youth Board may discuss or act on at this meeting.
The agenda packet consisting of minutes, staff reports and other documentation, is on file in the office of the Parks and
Recreation Department located at 150 N. Third St. and will be posted on the City's website at www.burbankca.gov. If
you have a question about any matter on the agenda, please call the office of the Parks and Recreation Department at
(818) 238-5300. The facility is disabled accessible. Auxiliary aids and services are available for individuals with speech,
vision, or hearing impairments (48-hour notice is required). Please contact the ADA Coordinator at (818) 238-5424 voice
or (818) 238-5035 TDD with questions or concerns.

Interpretation Requests: If you would like to participate in Public Comments and require an interpreter, please
telephone the City Clerk’s Office at (818) 238-5851 at least 48 hours in advance of the meeting.

Si desea participar en los comentarios públicos y necesita un intérprete, por favor llame a la Oficina de la Secretaria
Municipal al (818) 238-5851 al menos 48 horas antes de la reunión.

Public Comment Options: To speak during Public Comment, members of the public may speak for three minutes in-
person or connect by 6:00 p.m. if utilizing the zoom link: https://burbankca.zoom.us/j/88092163735. Members of the
public that attend the meeting will speak first followed by those on Zoom. If you experience difficulties connecting via
Zoom, you may also participate by calling 1 253 215 8782 and entering event number 880 9216 3735. Please note that
by choosing to participate via Zoom you will not have audio access to any portion of the meeting, you will be notified by
staff when you are connected with the Board Chair.

  A G E N D A

  A. CALL TO ORDER

  B. ROLL CALL

  C. PUBLIC COMMENT (Three minutes on matters concerning the Youth Board)

  D. RESPONSE TO ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

  E. APPROVAL OF MINUTES
 F. NEW BUSINESS
  1) Animal Shelter Presentation- Burbank Animal Shelter staff will provide an overview of the Animal
  Shelter and its services.

  2) Family Service Agency Presentation- Laurie Bleick and Taylor Foxhall will provide an overview of
  resources and services that the Family Service Agency (FSA) provides.

  3) Park, Recreation and Community Service Board Liaison Update
  The Board will receive a report from board liaisons.
  Recommendation: Note and file.

  4) Sustainable Burbank Commission Liaison Update
  The Board will receive a report from board liaisons.
  Recommendation: Note and file.

  5) Goals & Objectives
  The board will discuss and vote to determine goals and objectives for the 2025-2026 Youth Board
  term from the following topics;

  •Education and Career Exposure & Civic Education and Outreach : “Burbank Buzz”, social
  media campaign. Campaign includes: Youth & Government, Boys & Girls Club, Burbank
  Volunteer Program, Youth Employment, Rotary/Sunrise, Providence Volunteer Program and
  Sister City Committee.
  Recommendation: Discuss and take appropriate action.

  6) Teen Programming & Youth Leadership Program update
  The Board will receive a report from Staff regarding existing programs.
  Recommendation: Note and File.

  7) School Reports
  Each high school and middle school representative will give a brief report regarding respective
  school activities.

  Recommendation: The following reports are for information purposes only; and no action is
  required to be taken by the Board.

  A) Burbank High School
  B) Burroughs High School
  C) Providence High School
  D) Monterey High School
  E) Luther Burbank Middle School
  F) John Muir Middle School
  G) St. Finbar Middle School
  H) St. Francis Xavier Middle School
  I) St. Robert Bellarmine Middle School

  8) Personal Achievements and Recognitions
  Board members can voluntarily share any personal achievements and/or accomplishments with the
  group.

G. ADJOURNMENT
   BURBANK YOUTH BOARD MINUTES
  Wednesday, May 6, 2026

  A regular meeting of the Youth Board was held in the City of Burbank Community Services
  Building (CSB) Room #104, located at 150 N. Third St, Burbank, California. The meeting was
  called to order at 6:02 p.m. by Mr. Yoon, Chair.

ROLL CALL

PRESENT MEMBERS:  Brandon Chong, Tess Doty, Ghazal Eichoue, Emma Fernandez,
  Alice Greene, Kristina Kalustova, Daniel Lucha, Megan Ly, Michael
  Millunzi, Hannah Hope, O’Briant, Charlotte Pangman, Marianna
  Sergoyan, Aiden Yoon

ABSENT MEMBERS:  Tejas Deepak, Julia Hayes, Luke Smith

STAFF PRESENT:  Noah Altman, Recreation Manager
  Jenny Griffin, Recreation Supervisor
  Buster Roebuck, Senior Recreation Leader
  Christina Romero, Recording Secretary

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
None.

RESPONSE TO ORAL COMMUNICATIONS
None.

APPROVAL OF MINUTES
The Board approved the minutes from the April 1, 2026, meeting.

Action of the Board
Motioned by Mr. Yoon, seconded by Ms. Sergoyan, and carried 13-0 to approve April minutes.
 NEW BUSINESS

  Park, Recreation and Community Service Board Liaison
  Ms. Green provided a report.

  Action of the Board
  Noted and filed.

  Sustainable Burbank Commission Liaison
  Mr. Yoon provided a report.

  Action of the Board
  Noted and filed.

  Goals & Objectives
  The Board discussed and voted on goals and objectives for the 2025–26 Youth Board term:
  • Fundraising Donation Discussion:
  Ms. Griffin distributed copies of the fundraising donation flyers to Board
  members. The flyers are currently displayed at recreation centers, public
  libraries, and schools throughout the City. Ms. Griffin encouraged Board
  members to help spread the word. Funds raised from the Egg-Stravaganza
  fundraiser will be used to purchase items for the Animal Shelter. The fundraiser
  will run through Friday, May 29, 2026.
  • Education and Career Exposure and Civic Education and Outreach:
  The Board viewed a video submitted by a Board member to provide examples
  and guidance as additional videos continue to be submitted. Ms. Griffin asked
  the Board for updates regarding the progress of their film submissions. Mr.
  Altman encouraged members to submit their films, noting that the marketing
  team is available to assist with editing.
  Action of the Board
  Discussed, noted, and filed.
  Beautification Project
  Ms. Griffin discussed an opportunity from the Cultural Arts Commission regarding Phase
  10 of the Beautification Project

  The Board nominated Ms. Kalustova to serve as the Youth Board judge for the
  Beautification project.

  Action of the Board
  Motioned by Mr. Yoon, seconded by Ms. Sergoyan, and carried 13–0 to approve Ms.
  Kalustova as the Youth Board judge for the Beautification Project.
 Austin Cook Award for Outstanding Youth
Mr. Roebuck distributed twelve applications to the Board, and each application was read
aloud for review.
The Board collectively discussed the nominees and selected Nominee #2 to receive the
Austin Cook Award for Outstanding Youth. The selected nominee will be announced
during the May 19, 2026, City Council meeting.
Action of the Board
It was motioned by Mr. Yoon, seconded by Ms. Pangman, and carried 13–0 to approve
Nominee #2 to receive the Austin Cook Award for Outstanding Youth.

Teen Programming & Youth Leadership Program update
Mr. Roebuck gave a report on the Counselor in Training and Youth Leadership Program.

Action of the Board
Noted and filed.

Youth Board Calendar of Board Meetings
Ms. Griffin provided an update regarding the June 2026 meeting schedule. The Board
approved meeting in June.
Action of the Board
Motioned by Ms. Doty, seconded by Ms. Sergoyan, and carried 13–0 to approve a June
meeting.

School Reports
Each high school and middle school representative gave a brief report regarding
respective school activities.

Recommendation: The following reports are for information purposes only; and no action
is required to be taken by the Board.

  A) Burbank High School
  B) Burroughs High School
  C) Providence High School
  D) Monterey High School
  E) Luther Burbank Middle School
  F) John Muir Middle School
  G) St. Finbar Middle School
  H) St. Francis Xavier Middle School
  I) St. Robert Bellarmine

Personal Achievements and Recognitions
   Board members volunteered to share any personal achievements and/or
  accomplishments with the group.

Next meeting: June 3, 2026, at 6:00 p.m.

ADJOURNMENT
There being no further business to come before the Board, the meeting was adjourned at 7:43
p.m.
